validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE (checked far beyond the sheet's own citations, which rot on aptel.gov.in's https): this pipeline is exceptionally well documented as a real, formally authorized, and formally cancelled PNGRB common-carrier project. (1) PNGRB's own order dated 07.06.2022 (Order_JMPL_08.06.2022.pdf, 'In the matter of H-Energy Private Limited for Jaigarh-Mangalore Natural Gas Pipeline', pdftotext-confirmed -- the URL 200s but the automated substring screen can't read this PDF's compressed text streams at all, a documented false-negative for any compressed PDF, not a content problem) recounts the full regulatory history: authorization granted to HEPL 28.06.2016 under NGPL Authorisation Regulations 2008, original commissioning target 27.06.2019, PNGRB-approved extension to 31.03.2021, HEPL's own further (unapproved) request to push to May 2023, COVID disruption claimed from March 2020, project cost blown out from Rs 2389 crore to Rs 7865 crore, and progress assessed as 'nil' as of March 2022 -- ending with encashment of part of HEPL's performance bank guarantee as a first-default penalty. Notably this order also shows PARTIAL physical construction actually happened before the project died: 'Laying of 30 Km pipeline out of total 47 Km pipeline from Jaigarh to Hathkhamba' and '30 Km pipeline out of total 53 Km pipeline from Mangalore to Udupi' -- so this was not a paper-only proposal, real pipe went into the ground on two sub-sections before the whole 635-km project was killed. (2) APTEL Appeal No. 311 of 2022 (H-ENERGY PRIVATE LIMITED v. PNGRB, judgment pronounced 10.05.2023, aptel.gov.in/sites/default/files/Jud2023/A311of22_100523.pdf -- fetched via the working http:// scheme, pdftotext-confirmed) is H-Energy's OWN appeal against PNGRB's termination of the JMPL authorization. It lays out that HEPL itself had already sought to surrender the authorization ('It is not as if the Appellant intended to execute the JMPL project, if the authorization had been extended and not terminated' -- para 224), and that 'the Board passed an order on 04.07.2022, exercising its powers under the Act and Regulation 16(1)(c), and terminated the Authorisation of the Appellant for laying, building, operating or expanding the Jaigarh-Mangalore Natural Gas Pipeline' (para 51). The Tribunal's conclusion: 'The Appeal fails, and is accordingly dismissed' (para 228) -- i.e. an adversarial, litigated confirmation that the cancellation was valid, from the pipeline's own developer's failed challenge to it. This is about as strong as cancellation evidence gets. (3) A second, later APTEL judgment (Appeal Nos. 331/332/361 of 2022 etc., AGP CGD India/AGP City Gas v. PNGRB, dated 26.04.2024 -- a wholly different, unrelated litigant, the sheet's existing cited ref) independently references the same fact as settled background: 'JMPL was to be commissioned by June, 2019, but its authorization was cancelled by PNGRB vide order dated 4th July, 2022 which was upheld by this Tribunal vide judgement dated 10th May, 2023.' (4) Independent press: The Economic Times and Free Press Journal both ran the same PTI/Agencies wire story (9 June 2022) on the PNGRB fine -- 'HEPL was granted a licence to lay the 635-kilometer Jaigarh-Mangalore natural gas pipeline (JMPL) on June 28, 2016 ... capacity to carry 17 million standard cubic meters per day of gas ... supposed to be commissioned by June 27, 2019' -- this is one wire origin republished twice, so it counts as a single source per the standing rule, but it independently cross-checks (rather than originates) the regulatory-record facts above. (5) H-Energy's own archived corporate website (web.archive.org snapshot of henergy.com/natural-gas-pipeline-project/, Feb 2021) independently describes 'H-Energy is executing 635 km Jaigarh-Mangalore natural gas pipeline project on the West coast of India for which it has received authorization from Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) ... connect to the demand centres in the coastal towns/cities of Ratnagiri, Sindhudurg, Goa, Karwar, Udupi and Mangalore ... 1st phase of commissioning is expected by 2023.' Four independent origin types (regulator order, adversarial tribunal judgment, independent press, developer's own site) all agree this was a real, specific, well-defined project that was formally terminated, not a GEM-only or hallucinated entity. CLASSIFICATION: JMPL was authorized under the PNGRB (Authorizing Entities to Lay, Build, Operate or Expand Natural Gas Pipelines) Regulations, 2008 -- the NGPL/common-carrier transmission framework, explicitly distinct in both APTEL judgments from the separate CGD (city gas distribution) Authorization Regulations that govern local distribution networks. A 635-km trunk moving regasified LNG from one import terminal to feed multiple coastal city-gate/CGD networks across three states (Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka) is unambiguously transmission, not gathering/distribution -- classification confirmed. DUPLICATE CHECK vs the 13-row roster: none of the other 12 rows touch this west-coast Maharashtra-Goa-Karnataka corridor (they are all Rajasthan, West Bengal, Andhra Pradesh, or the cross-border IPI line) -- no overlap, no duplicate/relabel concern. Also checked against the operating GAIL Kochi-Koottanad-Bangalore-Mangalore Pipeline (KKBMPL), which also terminates near Mangalore and is referenced in the PNGRB order as a possible alternate gas source once JMPL was abandoned ('Connect Mangalore Goa section with GAIL's Kochi-Mangalore Natural Gas...') -- KKBMPL is a distinct, separate, already-operating pipeline from a different origin (Kochi, Kerala) and is not JMPL under another name.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: This is a CONFIRMED cancellation of the strongest kind available -- not a dormancy inference -- and closes one of the 8 blank-ShelvedCancelledType rows in this cluster. PNGRB terminated HEPL's authorization for JMPL by order dated 04.07.2022 under Regulation 16(1)(c) of the NGPL Authorisation Regulations 2008 (following an earlier 07.06.2022 order that had fined/encashed part of its performance bank guarantee for zero progress since March 2020). H-Energy itself appealed the termination (APTEL Appeal 311/2022) -- its own appeal was DISMISSED on 10.05.2023 ('The Appeal fails, and is accordingly dismissed'), and the Tribunal record shows H-Energy had ALREADY sought to surrender the authorization itself, i.e. the developer did not want to continue either. A second, unrelated litigant's APTEL judgment (26.04.2024) independently references the same 04.07.2022 cancellation as settled fact two years later, with no sign anywhere of a revival or re-authorization of JMPL under HEPL. Searched for any newer/contrary evidence: none found -- PNGRB's only subsequent activity on this west-coast corridor is unrelated (e.g. the operating GAIL KKBMPL line near Mangalore is a separate, pre-existing pipeline, not a JMPL revival). Status=cancelled stands confirmed; ShelvedCancelledType should move from blank to 'confirmed' (a source explicitly states the cancellation -- this is not our own dormancy inference) and CancelledYear=2022 (the 04.07.2022 termination order date) should be added, both currently blank on the sheet. Both PDFs cited 200 live (confirmed via the working http:// scheme, since aptel.gov.in's https certificate chain is broken site-wide) with content manually confirmed via pdftotext -- the automated substring screen cannot read either PDF's compressed text streams at all, a documented, unavoidable false-negative for this extractor on any real (non-plaintext) PDF, not a content or liveness problem.
